children: Insurance companies and pension funds are some of the most cautious money on the planet. Jeff Walton thinks some of that money could soon be headed toward Bitcoin.

Walton, Chief Risk Officer at Strive Inc. (NASDAQ: ASST), said on November 18, 2026 that institutional credit capital could shift away from financing AI data centers and into the Bitcoin market. He is not suggesting your grandmother's pension fund will start buying coins directly. He is pitching a different route.
Walton's argument starts with a simple observation about how AI gets built. According to Walton, nearly all AI data center build-outs today are financed with credit capital.

Walton's view is that this same credit could be redirected. Instead of funding server farms, it could fund Bitcoin exposure through instruments built specifically for investors who cannot hold digital assets outright.
That is where Strive's product lineup comes in. The company issues Bitcoin-collateralized perpetual preferred equity under two tickers: SATA and SATS.

For the uninitiated, perpetual preferred stock sits somewhere between a bond and a regular share. It pays a fixed dividend, has no maturity date, and ranks ahead of common stock if things go wrong. Strive backs these dividends with Bitcoin on its balance sheet.

The pitch to a pension fund manager is straightforward. You get a yield-paying security that looks familiar on paper, while the collateral underneath is Bitcoin. The fund never has to custody a single coin.
Strive's preferred shares advertise yields that would make a traditional fixed-income desk do a double take. SATA yields approximately 13%, while SATS yields around 15%, with dividends paid daily.
Daily payouts are an unusual feature. Most preferred stocks pay quarterly, so this is a deliberate design choice aimed at investors who want steady cash flow.
Demand has shown up, at least so far. Strive's recent SATS offering was oversubscribed and raised nearly $700 million.

The company has also used at-the-market (ATM) sales, which let a company sell shares gradually into the open market rather than in one big offering. In one such transaction, Strive sold $10M of SATS and used the proceeds to buy 250 BTC.
All of this feeds the company's Bitcoin treasury. Strive held between 32,000 and 43,000 BTC as of mid-to-late 2026, coins intended to back the dividends on its preferred shares.

Walton put the potential opportunity in large terms. He estimated that bringing Bitcoin-backed securities into rated credit markets could unlock anywhere from hundreds of billions up to $1 trillion in institutional capital.
That is a wide range. It is also a forecast from a company that would directly benefit if it came true, which is worth keeping in mind.
The framing here is clever. Walton is not asking institutions to abandon credit markets. He is asking them to consider a different borrower.

AI infrastructure has become a major destination for institutional lending. By positioning Bitcoin-backed preferred equity as an alternative use for that same capital, Strive is trying to compete for the exact dollars already flowing into tech build-outs.

The constraint Strive is solving for is regulatory and structural. Many insurers and pension funds operate under rules that keep them from holding digital assets directly. A preferred security collateralized by Bitcoin offers a workaround that fits inside their existing mandates, at least in principle.

For Strive, the strategy is a loop. Issue preferred shares, buy Bitcoin, use that Bitcoin to support dividends, then repeat. The oversubscribed SATS raise suggests appetite exists, and every successful issuance adds to the treasury.

The risks deserve equal billing. Yields in the 13% to 15% range are high for a reason. Investors are being compensated for taking on exposure to an asset that can swing sharply in price, and the collateral backing these dividends moves with Bitcoin.
The $1 trillion figure is an estimate of potential access, not committed capital.

title: Strive's Jeff Walton says institutional credit could pivot from AI data centers to Bitcoin
